# Modifier-Primacy Status - Repository vs. Specification

**What this document is:** a from-scratch audit of how far the current repository (`d:\Utilities\XAMPP\htdocs\dndchar`) is from `docs/architecture/modifier-primacy.md`, generated by checking each rule in that specification directly against the schema, service layer, types, and UI. Where the spec and this document disagree about what the target model *should be*, the spec wins - this document only reports distance to that target.

**Methodology:** originally checked against migrations 001-019 (the targeted edits below cover up to 049), `src/lib/server/services/*`, `src/lib/types/*`, `src/lib/rules/dnd5e.ts`, and the admin/character UI. This is a full regeneration, not an edit of any prior version. **Targeted edits since:** 2026-11-19 (VTT batch 2) corrected the advantage/disadvantage entries (§0, §2, §4, §7) against migrations up to 032 and `src/lib/rules/attackRoll.ts`, and added §4a's interim manual dice controls; everything else is still as of the original regeneration, so re-audit before trusting it elsewhere.

---

## 0. Things to flag before the findings

**Spec claims that assume something not true of the codebase:**
- §2.1 and the Open Questions list refer to **Soulfire** and **Vowfire** resource pools. As of migration 044 both exist (`resource_pool_definitions` rows plus `resource.soulfire.max` / `resource.vowfire.max` targets); this bullet used to say they did not.
- §5.2's worked example talks about "Rage (the class feature)" and "Raging (the state)" as two distinct things. The actual seed data has exactly one `Rage` row with its modifiers attached directly - there is no `Raging` entity. This implies content needs to be re-modeled as two pieces, not only that the engine needs a new capability.

---

## 1. Fully Conforms

Rules where the live code already does what the spec requires.

- **§2.1 - Modifier definition carries no duration, cost, or instance-source.** `modifier_definitions` holds only `target`, `modifier_type`, `default_value_expression`, `label`, `description`. Duration and cost live on the Container side.
- **§2.1 - Dot-notation target convention.** Confirmed throughout seed data and `modifier_targets`: `ability_check.str`, `attack_roll.all`, `damage_taken.bludgeoning`, etc.
- **§2.1 - Fixed and Dice value sources.** `default_value_expression` stores literal numbers and dice expressions; both are consumed correctly by the roll/bonus resolution code.
- **§2.2 - Empty-grant Containers (mundane inventory).** `character_inventory_items.source_content_id` is nullable, and freeform items are fully insertable with no mechanics attached.
- **§2.4 - Duration/lifecycle excluded from the Modifier.** `duration_type`, `duration_rounds`, `requires_concentration`, `expiry_boundary` all live on `content_definitions` (as of migration 019), never on `modifier_definitions`.
- **§3.1 - Flat numeric add/subtract sums normally.** `resolvedNumericModifiers` flat-maps every matching modifier's resolved value and sums them with no special-casing.
- **§4.2 - Mechanics always resolve against the live definition.** `resolveCharacterModifierSources` queries `modifier_definitions` directly every time; no mechanic text is frozen in snapshots.
- **§4.3 - Soft-delete only.** `is_archived` exists on `modifier_targets`, `modifier_definitions`, and `content_definitions`. No service code hard-deletes a definition row.
- **§4.5 - Update-in-place vs. fork-a-copy.** Both paths are real: `update` is gated behind a `confirmShared` checkbox server-side; `copy` forks a new independent definition.
- **§6.1 - Three-tier permission split.** `requireAdmin` in `hooks.server.ts` gates the `/admin` route prefix. `isAdmin` prop from `data.user?.role === 'admin'` gates all mechanical-authoring UI in the character sheet (Quick Add modal, Create Homebrew link, modifier attachment forms).
- **§6.2 - Authoring and applying separated in UI.** The Catalogue tab has been removed from the player-facing character sheet tab set. Catalogue browsing and authoring live exclusively in dedicated admin screens.
- **§6.3 - A Container may attach multiple independent Modifier instances.** `ContentTypeAdmin.svelte`'s repeatable `?/attachModifier` form adds one `content_modifier_links` row per submission; nothing limits a content record to a single modifier.
- **§6.4 - Two-phase roll resolution for outcome-dependent conditions.** Attack roll phase runs first; crit detection gates damage modifier conditions before the damage roll is computed.

- **§2.3 - Structured cost list and cost engine (cost-engine plan, migration 044, 2026-11-22).** `content_definitions.cost_json` is a list of `{pool, amount, ...}` lines (spell slot with a minimum level, own counter, item quantity, any resource pool) paid by `cost-engine.ts` at activation: casting, item use, weapon attacks and dashes. Every pay is atomic and takes locks in one fixed order (turn row first). Unaffordable costs go through the DM approval flow (`ask_dm` / `no_dm` / `dm_self`), every override is written to a resource ledger, and the DM can review and undo it.
- **§3.1 - Resource grants sum by count.** Character resource pools (`resource_pool_definitions`, e.g. Soulfire, Vowfire) take their maxima from `bonus`/`penalty` modifiers on `resource.<key>.max`, summed by count with a source-attributed breakdown. The per-turn action pools do the same on `action_pool.<key>.max`, and Extra Attack-style follow-ups on `followup.<type>.count`.
- **§2.3 - The character's own action economy is a target (action-economy plan, migration 045, 2026-11-22).** Two built-in profiles (`dnd5e`: Action / Bonus action / Reaction; `attack_utility`: 2 Attack + 2 Utility, homebrew), chosen per campaign. Cost lines carry a timing and a category and the profile maps them to a pool. Per-turn spend lives in `character_turn_state`. A weapon attack, a dash, spells and items all charge it. Free follow-ups (Extra Attack, spell echoes) and manual resets (sheet Next Turn / Round / New Battle, VTT Reset and Reset all) are built. The VTT shows the remaining actions on the token and offers a dash when the owning player moves past their movement.

## 2. Partially Conforms (Needs Reshaping)

Rules where a real, working piece of the mechanism exists, but it is incomplete or scoped too narrowly.

- **§2.1 - Modifier target categories.** Derived stats, roll categories, and discrete rules are all real and seeded. Resource-pool targets are real now: `resource.<key>.max` per character pool (Soulfire, Vowfire and DM-defined ones), `action_pool.<key>.max` and `followup.<type>.count` (see §1).
- **§2.1 - Stat-derived formula value source.** `modifier_targets.value_kind` declares a `formula` kind, but `resolveModifierNumericValue` (`dnd5e.ts`) only evaluates one hardcoded literal (`rage_damage_bonus`). No general formula evaluator exists.
- **§2.2 - Per-instance Container parameters (decks unit 2, 2026-11-23).** A grant can now carry parameter values for one particular application: `applyCharacterEffect` writes `metadata_json.params` (plus a `sourceLabel`) on the `active_character_effects` row, and link expressions use `{name}` placeholders that `substituteParams` fills in before `mapModifier` (a missing name is 0; pure integer `+`/`-` arithmetic is folded, dice are left alone). A condition with no placeholders behaves exactly as before, and the label is appended to the source name so every `?` breakdown shows which application it came from. Only applied conditions have this so far: items, feats and other grant paths still take their values from the link or definition alone.
- **§2.2 - Container field completeness.** Migration 019 added `activation_type`, `cost_json`, `duration_type`, `duration_rounds`, `requires_concentration`, `expiry_boundary`, `stack_behavior` to `content_definitions`. These fields are present but the **service layer** (catalogue.ts, characters.ts) does not yet read or honour `cost_json` or `activation_type` declaratively - cost is still handled procedurally per content type. The schema is right; the engine hasn't caught up.
- **§2.5 - Source and target-of-effect tracked independently.** Now exercised (decks, 2026-11-23): `applyCharacterEffect` takes `sourceCharacterId`, and a deck draw writes the drawer as `source_character_id` on every effect it puts on a party member. It is stored and shown in labels, but the engine doesn't yet resolve anything differently by source character. Snapshots keep `metadata_json` but not `source_character_id` (accepted, commented in the code). There is still no menu-driven "grant a buff to another character" UI.
- **§2.6 - Audit trail for every resolved value.** Real and working for attack rolls and damage (`rollDamageExpression` builds a labelled breakdown). AC, skill checks, saving throws have `?` formula modals with source attribution. Not uniformly structured as a reusable audit-trail type - each value implements its own breakdown independently. A first reusable piece now exists for the 9 overridable combat-summary/magic stats specifically: `resolveCharacterStats()` (`src/lib/rules/characterStats.ts`) is the single resolver for Proficiency/AC/Initiative/Speed/the three Passives/Spell Save DC/Spell Attack Bonus, and its `manualOverrideLines`/`withManualLines` helpers generate the manual-override portion of each stat's `?` breakdown uniformly. Saves, skills, and other rolls still build their own breakdown text independently. Senses (vision, darkvision, truesight, devil's sight) now also have a source-attributed breakdown (`resolveSense`/`visionBreakdown` in `dnd5e.ts`), shown via a `?` modal in the sheet's Combat Summary.
- **§3.1 - Stacking by operation type: `minimum` (highest wins) op.** The `minimum` op ("At least - highest wins") exists in `ModifierOperation` and `operationRegistry`, and the spec's §3.1 table has a matching row (user-approved 2026-11-19). Only senses (`vision.*_ft`) honour it so far; on any other target it does nothing. Added 2026-11-19 (VTT batch 2: darkvision).
- **§3.1 - Advantage/disadvantage - one bucket per roll, all origins stacking by count.** `rollWithModifiers` (`attackRoll.ts`) counts every advantage and disadvantage source individually (attacker modifiers, target modifiers, token conditions, and the manual situational counters), nets them in the roll's single bucket via `resolveDicePool`, and rolls the real 1+|net| pool. Each source is listed in the audit text and can be unticked before rolling. Not yet modelled: per-bucket scoping beyond the roll's own candidate list (e.g. separate buckets for attacks versus saves are separate rolls, not separate pools within one roll). Conditions now reach VTT attack rolls via their Containers (Invisible and Frightened also affect sheet attack rolls, and Frightened sheet ability checks; migration 032 seeds the mechanics, including the new `attacks_against.*` targets; the VTT resolves `token.conditions` through `loadVttConditionEffects`).
- **§5.1 - Containers granting Containers.** `content_grants` exists and is joined in `resolveCharacterModifierSources` (branch 4). Migration 019 populates it with effect-as-Container grants from `content_effect_links`. One hop only - no recursive grant chain walking yet.

## 3. Missing Entirely

Rules with no trace anywhere in schema, services, or UI.

- **§2.1 - Derived-from-sibling value source.** No column, no resolver branch. Crit-bonus damage derived from a weapon's own base die doesn't exist in any form.
- **§2.4 - Expiry side-effects as a grant-on-trigger.** No `on_expire` trigger type. A Container that fires something specific when it wears off (spec's Haste-lethargy example) has no mechanism.
- **§3.1 - Resistance/vulnerability per-damage-type netting.** No code nets resistance against vulnerability per damage type.
- **§3.1 - "Doesn't stack with itself" flag.** No per-modifier-definition boolean for this. The adjacent `effect_definitions.stack_behavior` enum controls re-application behaviour, not modifier-level stacking exceptions.
- **§4.4 - Version-history drift display.** `VersionList.svelte` renders a label and a restore button only. No logic distinguishes character-state diffs from modifier-definition drift. No drift display at all. This now has a second dimension worth flagging once it's built: `statOverrides` (see §4a) are frozen/restored as character state, but a stored `override` value can silently mask a computed value that has since changed (e.g. the underlying rules/items changed since the override was set). The future drift view should flag when an override is hiding a computed value that no longer matches what was true when the override was set - not just modifier-definition drift.
- **Magic system - concentration state tracking.** `spell_definitions.concentration` is a boolean metadata field only. No mechanism enforces the "only one concentration spell at a time" rule or applies the concentration Container to the character when a spell is cast.
- **Content/inventory resource maxima don't recompute on a proficiency override, adjustment, or level change.** `initializeContentResources`/`initializeInventoryResources` (`catalogue.ts`) resolve `max_value_expression` (including `proficiency_bonus`) once, at the moment content is added or its resource definition is edited - via `effectiveProficiencyBonus()` (`characterStats.ts`), so it does respect an override/adjustment set *at that moment*. Neither function re-runs when the override/adjustment changes afterwards or when the character levels up, so an already-initialized pool's max can go stale until content is re-added or edited. Accepted as-is; a follow-up to recompute would need a trigger point (e.g. on save) that doesn't exist yet.

## 4. Direct Conflicts

Rules where the current code actively does something different from what the spec requires.

- **§2.2 - Unified Container concept - in progress (migration 019).** The live schema now has `content_definitions` extended with Container-level fields, and `effect_definitions` and `action_definitions` have been migrated into `content_definitions` as `content_type = 'condition'` and `content_type = 'action'` respectively. The rule engine's branch 1 (previously `effect_definitions → effect_modifier_links`) now routes through `container_id → content_definitions → content_modifier_links` for all active character effects. **The old tables (`effect_definitions`, `action_definitions`, `content_effect_links`) are preserved for now as read-only legacy.** Service-layer code (`catalogue.ts`, `characters.ts`, `effects.ts`) still writes to the old tables - updating these services to write to `content_definitions` directly is the remaining work for this conflict.

*(None currently recorded against the advantage rule - the former §3.1 cancellation conflict is resolved, see §7.)*

## 4a. Deliberate Deviations (Accepted)

Rules where the code intentionally does not follow the spec's letter, by a decision recorded during planning rather than an oversight.

- **Manual sheet-stat overrides live in `characters.metadata_json.statOverrides`, not as Modifier grants.** The 9 overridable combat-summary/magic stats (Proficiency, AC, Initiative, Speed, the three Passives, Spell Save DC, Spell Attack Bonus) each accept a player-typed adjustment and a hard override, resolved by the single reusable `resolveCharacterStats()` (`src/lib/rules/characterStats.ts`). This is a deliberate departure from "Modifier is the only mechanical primitive" (see overridable-sheet-stats plan). Reasons:
  - **§6.1 permissions.** Attaching a grant to a Container is DM/admin-gated. A manual override is character state a player types in (the same class as current HP), not authored mechanics - forcing it through the Container/grant path would either break the permission model or require a new "player-authored" carve-out the spec doesn't have.
  - **Not a reusable mechanic.** A manual override isn't a shared definition referenced by multiple characters (unlike `luck_dice`) - it's a one-off number for one character.
  - **§8's open 'set' tie-break sidestepped.** Manual overrides sit outside the modifier engine entirely, so they don't need to resolve against §8's still-open question of how competing `set` modifiers should rank.
  - **`proficiency_bonus` isn't a modifier target.** Proficiency comes straight from `proficiencyBonus(level)`, not from resolved Modifier instances, so a Proficiency override has nothing to attach to inside the engine as it exists today.
  - **Precedence:** the manual *adjustment* is summed into the computed pipeline BEFORE any `set`-type modifier (a `set`, e.g. Grappled's `speed.all set 0`, discards the adjustment along with the rest of the base). The manual *override* is final and beats everything, `set` included. Speed is the only one of the 9 stats whose resolver honours `set` today; for the other 8, the adjustment is simply one more additive term (see `speedPipeline`'s header comment in `dnd5e.ts` for the exact order of operations).
  - Both the adjustment and the override show up as labelled lines in the `?` formula-help audit trail (`manualOverrideLines`/`withManualLines`), so §2.6's audit-trail expectation still holds even though the value isn't Modifier-sourced.
  - Overrides are frozen and restored by character version snapshots exactly like any other `metadata_json` field (`buildSnapshot`/`applySnapshot` already capture the whole row) - so they behave like character state for history purposes, per §4.1.

- **Manual situational adv/dis counters and manual damage dice are per-roll parameters, not Modifiers (INTERIM, added 2026-11-19, VTT batch 2).** The pre-roll panels (the sheet's `RollOptionsModal.svelte` and the VTT attack confirm card) offer two things that are deliberately not part of the modifier model:
  - **Situational advantage/disadvantage counters (0-5 each).** These feed the same dice-pool netting as every other source and are labelled "Situational (manual)" in the audit trail. They are plain `RollChoices` values, never `modifierSources`.
  - **A manual damage-dice delta (-5..+5)** applied to the primary damage dice (`adjustPrimaryDamageDice`), on weapons, spells, manual attacks, items and heals.
  - **Why:** the user wanted a quick stopgap at the table before proper modifiers for extra damage dice exist. They introduce no `modifier_definitions` rows, targets or op types, and every piece carries an `// INTERIM:` comment. To be replaced by real modifiers later; at that point the delete-list is those comments.

- **Homebrew crit rule: max of the primary damage dice, added once (added 2026-11-19).** On a critical hit the damage dice are rolled normally, then the maximum of the weapon's/spell's own primary dice is added once on top (2d8 + 1d4 poison + 4 becomes 2d8 + 1d4 + 4 + 16; nothing is doubled, flat bonuses and secondary/extra dice are not maximised). Primary dice = the first die size in the expression, merged, same rule as the interim manual damage-dice control. This is a deliberate homebrew departure from 5e's double-the-dice rule. It is hard-coded in `critMaxDiceBonus` (`dnd5e.ts`) and applied by `rollDamage` whenever the hit's outcomes include `critical_hit`, covering the primary dice after any INTERIM manual adjustment (not sneak attack or other extra dice), for sheet and VTT weapon and spell attacks. It is not a Modifier, so it isn't DM-configurable yet; making it one (e.g. a crit-damage rule target) is future work.

- **Decks (2026-11-23): deliberate choices.** A deck is a Container (`content_definitions` type `deck` plus a 1:1 `deck_definitions` rules row; campaign-owned or global via `deck_definitions.campaign_id`). Its cards, tag-match success table and outcome templates are data. Its effects are ordinary condition Containers with modifier links, so the modifier-primacy rule holds for everything a deck grants.
  - **Decks have their own applier, not `action_steps`.** The deck applier (`services/decks.ts`, pure helpers in `src/lib/rules/decks.ts`) is modelled on `applyResourceChange`. Action steps can't express what a deck needs: `{value}` taken from the drawn card, targets other than self (each party member, an even split with the remainder to the drawer), shared rolls across the party, and inverting every step on a failure. Bolting those onto `action_steps` would have bent a self-only model for one feature. What a deck does reuse is the Container machinery: conditions applied through `applyCharacterEffect` with per-instance params (§2.2) and `source_character_id` (§2.5).
  - **Deck temp HP stacks.** A gain adds on top of existing temp HP, and a failure removes that amount, floored at 0. This is a deliberate homebrew departure from 5e's keep-the-higher rule (user decision, Rev 3 Q3), and it matches the existing `resource_change` temp HP add. Deck damage takes temp HP first and has no damage type, so resistances don't apply.
  - **VTT token AC follows the sheet AC by the size of each change.** `token.sheetAc` is the sheet AC a PC token last followed. When the resolved sheet AC moves, the token's AC moves by the same amount from wherever it is (`vttTokenAc.ts`, `followSheetAc`), so a GM's manual offset is kept. This replaces the old "token AC never follows the sheet" rule and is why a condition's AC modifier now reaches VTT defence (which uses `token.ac`). It follows any sheet AC change, not just deck ones.
  - **Draws store ids, tags and applied deltas only** (presence is historical, mechanics current, §4.1). Undo reverses what was actually applied, clamped, and notes anything it couldn't fully reverse.
  - **Two outcomes are DM prompts, not mechanics:** resistance or vulnerability to a chosen damage type, and cure-one-condition, plus the magic item, enemy, ally and cursed item results.
  - **Authoring follows the campaign** (a DM-created deck is campaign-owned, global decks come from seeds and are read-only, copy to edit). Conditions a deck uses must be global for now. Homebrew-library sharing comes later.
- **Action economy (2026-11-22): deliberate choices.**
  - **Profiles are built in, in code** (`src/lib/rules/actionEconomy.ts`), not DM-editable data: the mapping is logic (by timing in 5e, by category in the homebrew profile). Cost lines carry tags, not pool names, so an editable profile table can be added later without touching content.
  - **Turn state lives outside `resource_pool_definitions`** (`character_turn_state`, storing what was SPENT this turn). Pool definitions are global but turn pools depend on the campaign's profile, rests and the Save/replace code don't know a "turn" period, and a snapshot restore must not time-travel "spent an Attack this turn".
  - **Turn lines are inherited separately from resource lines.** NULL `cost_json` is the full default; an explicit list without a turn line keeps its own resources and still takes the default action line; a turn line with timing Free is how an author makes something take no action.
  - **A normal turn spend is not ledgered** (it resets every turn); the turn row's own log is the audit trail. Overrides do get ledger rows.
  - **Resets are manual** (no initiative tracker), and movement within speed is free; only going past it (a dash) costs a general action.
  - **`token.turn` is a display copy** pushed by the owner's client and rebuilt server-side (`sanitizeTurn`); every change goes through HTTP. A token whose owner is not connected shows a stale copy until they join.
  - **Not in the modifier model:** the dash itself (a built-in activation, not a granted action) and the 5e bonus-action-spell restriction.

## 5. Magic System - Design Requirements

The magic system is the largest single feature gap from a player-experience standpoint. It overlaps significantly with the Container unification (spells are Containers) and the cost engine (spell slot costs are structured costs). This section documents the design requirements so they can be implemented alongside the Container work.

### 5.1 What the spec says about spells

Spells are Containers. There is no special "Spell" entity type in the architecture - a spell is a named Container with an `activation_type` of `active_use`, `cost_json` that declares its slot level and amount, and optional grants (Containers or Modifiers that activate while the spell is in effect). This is the same shape as a class feature, a feat, or a condition - only the metadata differs.

### 5.2 Spell-specific metadata (retained from `spell_definitions`)

These fields are spell-flavour metadata, not new mechanical concepts:
- `spell_level` (0-9) - determines minimum slot level
- `school` - flavour only
- `casting_time` - action economy source: maps to `cost_json` pool `action`, `bonus_action`, or `reaction`
- `range`, `components`, `duration`, `ritual`, `higher_level` - flavour/reference only
- `concentration` - determines whether the Container sets `requires_concentration = true`; enforced by the cost engine when the spell is cast
- `classes` - determines who can learn it

### 5.3 What needs designing (currently open)

**Concentration enforcement:** When a concentration spell is activated, any previously active Container with `requires_concentration = true` on the same character must be deactivated. This is a rule in the cost/activation engine, not in the Container definition itself.

**Upcasting:** A spell may be cast at a higher slot level than its minimum. The cast-level choice changes the `cost_json` amount deducted. The spell's `higher_level` text describes the upcast benefit; the mechanical expression of that benefit (extra damage dice, extended duration, etc.) is currently only text - it needs to be Modifier instances gated on `condition_expression: 'cast_level >= N'`.

**Ritual casting:** An alternate activation path with no slot cost but a +10-minute casting time. Not representable as `cost_json = []` alone (zero cost spells currently have no way to declare the time cost). A `ritual: true` flag on the spell Container's metadata plus an alternate activation path in the engine.

**Cantrips (level 0):** `spell_level = 0`, `cost_json = []` (no slot). Cantrip damage scaling by level (the 5e rule where cantrips deal more damage at character level 5/11/17) is a Modifier gated on a character-level condition - currently not expressible because no condition type for "character total level >= N" exists in `modifierConditionMatches`.

**Prepared vs. known spells:** Wizards prepare from a known list; Warlocks know and always have prepared; Clerics/Druids have always-prepared domain spells plus a daily preparation. The `is_known` / `is_prepared` flags on `character_content_instances` already exist; the preparation rules per class are not enforced anywhere and need explicit per-class logic.

**Spell attack rolls:** `content_definitions` rows for spells that require an attack roll need a Modifier instance on `spell_attack_roll` (type `bonus`, value `proficiency_bonus + spellcasting_ability_modifier`). This is already expressible; the existing seed data may be incomplete.

### 5.4 Spell slots - current state vs. target

Current: `character_spell_slots` (separate table), decremented directly in `castCharacterSpell`.

Target: Spell slots are just character resource pools - `character_resources` entries with `resource_key = 'spell_slot_1'` through `spell_slot_9`, plus `pact_slot_1`-`pact_slot_9` for Warlocks. The cost engine reads `cost_json` from the spell Container and deducts from the matching pool. `character_spell_slots` becomes legacy once this migration is complete.

This is a significant migration (removing a dedicated table, replacing with generic resource pools) and should be treated as a separate task after the cost engine is in place.

## 6. Container Unification - Current Progress and Remaining Work

*§6 re-audited 2026-11-21 against `vttpoc` (`7de8dea6`). Only this section was regenerated - the rest of the document is still dated 2026-11-19. The migration plan lives at `~/.claude/plans/dndchar/container-migration/container-migration.md`.*

### 6.1 What migration 019 accomplished

- `content_definitions` now carries all Container-level fields: `activation_type`, `cost_json`, `duration_type`, `duration_rounds`, `requires_concentration`, `expiry_boundary`, `stack_behavior`, `is_system`.
- `content_type` now accepts `'condition'` and `'action'` in addition to the original four.
- `effect_definitions` rows were copied into `content_definitions` as `content_type = 'condition'` (key `condition:<effect_key>`). Not copied: `source_type`, `source_ref`, `is_condition`, `is_selectable`, `is_homebrew`, `sort_order`, `metadata_json`, `owner_user_id`. The legacy `duration_type` was mapped lossily into the new vocabulary.
- `effect_modifier_links` were copied into `content_modifier_links`. `content_effect_links` were copied into `content_grants`.
- `action_definitions` were copied into `content_definitions` as `content_type = 'action'` (key `action:<action_key>`).
- Added `container_id` to `active_character_effects` and `action_steps`, and `action_container_id` to `content_action_links` (not `container_id`). All three were back-filled. `action_steps.effect_id` (a legacy effect reference) got **no** container equivalent.
- The rule engine's branch 1 reads via `container_id`, with a legacy fallback (`rule-engine.ts:52-64`) for `container_id IS NULL`.
- Since 019, some condition mechanics exist **only** on the container side: migration 032 added 15 `content_modifier_links` on condition Containers with no `effect_modifier_links` twin. So the legacy tables are no longer a complete picture.

### 6.2 Remaining legacy reads/writes (audit 2026-11-21)

Schema blockers: `active_character_effects.effect_id`, `action_steps.action_id` and `content_action_links.action_id` are still `NOT NULL`, so no write path can go container-only yet.

| action-engine.ts:44-49 | R | `step.effect_id` (legacy id) -> apply/removeCharacterEffect |
| catalogue.ts:39-43 | R | listCatalogue effects: `content_effect_links` ⋈ `effect_definitions` |
| catalogue.ts:179-189 | W | attachEffectToContent dual-writes `content_effect_links` + `content_grants` |
| catalogue.ts:204-224 | W | attachEffectToOwnedContent on_use: `action_definitions`, `content_action_links.action_id`, `action_steps(action_id, effect_id)`. Bug: a repeat attach nulls `action_container_id` |

No direct legacy SQL in `src/routes`, `vtt/`, `server.js` or `vttConditions.ts` (already container-keyed).

Drift risk: the legacy-only write paths above (content-admin actions and effect attach, scripts) can have created rows since 019 that have no container twin or have NULL container columns. On the local dev DB (2026-11-21) every drift count is 0. Prod is unchecked - the plan's read-only check query covers it.

### 6.3 Tables/columns to drop once 6.2 is empty

- `effect_definitions`, `effect_modifier_links`, `effect_sources`, `content_effect_links`, `action_definitions`
- `active_character_effects.effect_id`, `action_steps.effect_id` (needs a new `effect_container_id` first), `action_steps.action_id`, `content_action_links.action_id`

Don't drop these until every 6.2 row is gone, a re-run backfill has passed its guards, and the app has been through at least one real session on the container-only code.

## 7. What changed since the prior version of this document

- **2026-11-23 - decks (targeted edit, units 1-9b).** §2.5 moved on from "schema only": `source_character_id` is written by deck effects. New §2 entry for per-instance Container parameters (`metadata_json.params`, `{name}` placeholders). §4a gains the decks entry (own applier instead of `action_steps`, stacking temp HP, `sheetAc` delta-follow for VTT token AC). New condition expiry `next_attack` (migration 046). Migrations 046-049 (next-attack expiry, deck schema, the Deck of Mystical Fate seed, campaign-owned decks) must be run with `npm run db:migrate:prod` before the deploy that needs them. Nothing else was re-audited.

- **2026-11-22 - cost engine and action economy.** Moved to §1: the structured cost list and engine (§2.3), resource grants summing by count (§3.1) and the character's action economy as a target (§2.3). Removed the four now-false "missing" entries (cost engine, structured cost list, spell-slot cost engine, resource-grant sums). §4a records the deliberate action economy choices. §0's Soulfire/Vowfire bullet is corrected (both are seeded by migration 044 with resource.<key>.max targets). Still open: the VTT has no spell echo choice yet.

- **2026-11-19, VTT batch 2 (advantage):** the §0 bullet claiming the code used binary cancellation and the §4 "cancellation rule" conflict were already false (the dice pool was wired on 2026-06-30, `5da2ab88`) and are removed. `resolveAdvantageState` derives from the pool's net, and `rollWithModifiers` rolls the real pool for every d20 roll. The §2 per-bucket scoping entry is rewritten (all origins stack by count in one bucket). See also §4a for the interim manual dice controls.

- **§6.1 Permission tiers** - moved from §3 Missing Entirely to §1 Fully Conforms. `requireAdmin` guards `/admin` routes; `isAdmin` prop gates all mechanical-authoring UI.
- **§6.2 Catalogue tab separation** - moved from §4 Direct Conflicts to §1 Fully Conforms. The Catalogue tab no longer appears on the player-facing character sheet.
- **§6.4 Two-phase roll resolution** - moved from §3 Missing Entirely to §1 Fully Conforms.
- **§2.2 Container unification** - status changed from "Direct Conflict - not started" to "Direct Conflict - in progress." Migration 019 ran; schema extended; rule engine branch 1 updated. Service-layer migration is the remaining work.
- **Hit dice management** - per-class hit dice pools (`hit_dice_0`, `hit_dice_1`, ...) added to `character_resources`, tracked via index-based keys to avoid class name conflicts. `spendHitDice` action and `useHitDie` client function implement HP recovery with CON modifier and headroom capping. Short/long rest restoration of hit dice pools is deferred (see §3 pending items).
- **Formula audit modals** - `?` help buttons on all derived values (AC, proficiency, saves, skills, initiative, speed, spell DC, spell attack) open a modal showing source-attributed breakdown. Not yet a unified audit-trail type, but uniformly present.
- **Overridable sheet stats** - Proficiency, AC, Initiative, Speed, the three Passives, Spell Save DC, and Spell Attack Bonus are now directly editable (a manual adjustment plus a hard override), stored in `metadata_json.statOverrides` rather than as Modifier grants (see new §4a for why). Resolved by the shared `resolveCharacterStats()`/`characterStatsFor()` (`src/lib/rules/characterStats.ts`), used by the sheet, `/vtt/api/characters/[id]`, and the VTT's `roll-attack`/`roll-spell` endpoints alike, so a manual override/adjustment on the sheet now reaches every consumer instead of only affecting what the sheet displayed. Per-class hit dice pools (current and max) are now directly editable too, instead of a read-only summary; `spendHitDice` no longer overwrites an existing pool's `max_value`. Fixed a pre-existing double-count bug along the way: `rollWithModifiers` was adding a roll's flat bonus/penalty modifiers a second time for saves/skills/initiative, which also would have let those double-counted modifiers silently out-rank a manual override.
- **2026-11-19 - VTT batch 2: darkvision.** Added the `minimum` op (senses only) and the §3.1 table row, the `resolveSense`/`visionBreakdown` audit trail, the sheet's read-only Senses line, and the VTT `sheetVision` compare-and-follow sync. This is a targeted edit only; the stale §0/§4 advantage/disadvantage text is still to be corrected (batch 2's advantage unit, or the full regeneration).
